title: OS Grokbot Launches: Run Claude, Codex in Self-Hosted Agent
summary: OS Grokbot is a provider-agnostic, locally hostable agent wrapper for Claude, Codex, and more. Built for long-term tasks and operational workflows.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OS Grokbot is a self-hosted, provider-agnostic agent that wraps Claude, Codex, and other AI subscriptions into tmux terminals.
- Designed for long-term tasks, business workflows, and operational work, with full local control over data and infrastructure.
- Officially launched on November 7, 2026, available now at qorqbot.com with open-source architecture for enterprise and developer use.


A new self-hosted AI agent platform has arrived for developers and enterprises seeking full control over their Claude, Codex, and other AI subscriptions. OS Grokbot, officially launched on November 7, 2026, is a provider-agnostic wrapper that integrates directly into tmux-based terminal environments, enabling long-term task execution and operational workflows without relying on external cloud infrastructure. The tool is designed to give teams the flexibility to run their existing AI subscriptions locally while maintaining complete data sovereignty.


## What OS Grokbot Does


OS Grokbot acts as a terminal-native orchestration layer for multiple AI providers. Instead of forcing users into a single vendor ecosystem, the platform allows teams to plug in their existing Claude or Codex subscriptions and run them through a unified, locally controlled interface. The tmux integration means agents can persist across sessions, maintain context over extended periods, and handle multi-step workflows that span hours or days. This design prioritizes operational reliability and business process automation over one-off queries.


The architecture is built to be entirely locally hostable, meaning organizations can deploy the system on their own infrastructure without sending data to external APIs beyond the AI provider calls themselves. This is particularly relevant for teams working with sensitive codebases, proprietary data, or regulated industries where cloud-based agent platforms pose compliance risks.


## Long-Term Task Execution and Business Workflows


According to the project team, OS Grokbot excels at sustained operational work. The platform is optimized for scenarios where AI agents need to maintain state, execute multi-phase tasks, and integrate with existing development and operations tooling. Example use cases include continuous code review pipelines, incident response automation, and iterative refactoring projects that require persistent context across multiple terminal sessions.


- Provider-agnostic design supports Claude, Codex, and future AI subscription services
- Tmux-native architecture for persistent, long-running agent sessions
- Fully self-hosted deployment with no external dependencies beyond AI API calls
- Designed for operational workflows, not conversational chat


## Availability and Open Source Status


OS Grokbot is available now at qorqbot.com, with full documentation and setup instructions for local deployment. The project is positioned as an open-source alternative to proprietary agent platforms, though the team has not yet published formal benchmarks comparing its performance to existing tools. The Hacker News community response has been cautiously optimistic, with early adopters noting the appeal of a self-hosted approach for enterprise environments where data control is non-negotiable.


## What This Means


OS Grokbot represents a meaningful step toward decentralized AI agent infrastructure. By decoupling agent orchestration from vendor-specific platforms, the tool gives developers and operations teams the ability to leverage their existing AI subscriptions without sacrificing control over data, deployment, or long-term task continuity. As organizations increasingly demand on-premises or hybrid AI solutions, tools like OS Grokbot will likely become a critical part of the enterprise AI stack, particularly for teams that need to run Claude, Codex, or other models in regulated or high-security environments.
